FINDINGS:   Lower thorax: Right lower lobe periosteophyte stranding. Linear  scarring versus atelectasis in the lung bases.   Liver and biliary tree: Diffuse hepatic steatosis, mild in severity.  Previously described hypoattenuating lesion, possibly hemangioma  within the right hepatic lobe is difficult to visualize given the  background of diffuse fatty infiltration. No biliary ductal  dilatation.   Gallbladder: Dependent density could represent sludge or tiny stones.  No evidence of cholecystitis.   Spleen: Normal.   Pancreas: Mild fatty atrophy of the head and body.   Adrenal glands: Normal.   Kidneys and ureters: Severe atrophy of the right kidney. Previously  described layering hyperdense material in the right renal collecting  system not well seen on this exam. Urothelial thickening persists.  Similar-appearing hypoattenuating lesions in the left kidney.  Unchanged nonobstructing calculi in the left kidney lower pole  collecting system measuring up to 12 mm (6-277). No evidence of  hydronephrosis. Similar-appearing perinephric stranding on the left,  nonspecific. The left kidney appears to enhance and excrete contrast  normally. There is minimal excretion of contrast on the right.   Gastrointestinal tract: Status post sleeve gastrectomy. No evidence  of bowel obstruction. The appendix is surgically absent.   Peritoneal cavity: No free fluid.   Bladder: Normal.   Prostate and seminal vesicles: Normal.   Vasculature: Patent.   Lymph nodes: Mildly enlarged porta hepatis lymph node measuring 1.3  cm in the short axis and retrocaval lymph node measuring 1.1 cm in  short axis, stable compared to prior, likely reactive. Prominent  bilateral inguinal lymph nodes.   Abdominal wall: Minimal infiltrative changes seen within the anterior  abdominal wall subcutaneous soft tissues.   Musculoskeletal: Degenerative change of the spine. Please refer to  the dedicated CT of the lumbar spine for more detailed evaluation.
1.  Part of the abdominal wall is excluded from the field of view.
2.  No acute traumatic findings within the abdomen or pelvis. Please  refer to the dedicated CT of the lumbar spine for more detailed  evaluation.
3.  Similar-appearing severely atrophic right kidney with minimal  excretion of contrast and suggestion of urothelial thickening,  probably chronic in nature. Previously identified layering debris  within the right ureter not well seen on today's examination.
4.  Unchanged nonobstructive left kidney lower pole nephrolithiasis.
5.  Hepatomegaly measuring 17.8 cm in the craniocaudal dimension with  mild steatosis. Previously described hypoattenuating lesion within  the right hepatic lobe, possibly a hemangioma is not well seen given  the background of fatty infiltration.
